Connect to a store

Source: R/connect.R
store_connect.Rd

Reads the catalogs of the primary location and of every secondary one and returns the connection object. Nothing about the connection is saved: each script, or the environment of the session, decides which locations it has.

Usage

store_connect(
  primary = NULL,
  secondary = NULL,
  env = "STORE",
  history = NULL,
  create = FALSE,
  auth = NULL
)

Arguments

primary

Address of the primary location, the source of truth. NULL reads it from the environment variable <env>_PRIMARY.

secondary

Addresses of secondary locations, a character vector, in the order in which writes reach them. NULL reads them from <env>_SECONDARY when primary is NULL too, and means none otherwise.

env

Prefix of the environment variables, "STORE" by default.

history

Whether writes of this connection keep earlier versions: TRUE or FALSE override the store's default (set by store_create()); NULL uses it. A dataset's own setting, given to store_write(), overrides both.

create

TRUE initialises locations that hold no catalogs yet.

auth

Credentials for Google Cloud Storage locations (local folders need none): NULL uses rcs_auth_gcs(), the default lookup; an object made by rcs_auth_gcs() applies to every GCS location; a string is the path of a key file; a list named by address (as given in the call) gives each location any of these, and locations left out use the default.

Value

An object of class rcs_store. Print it to see its locations and datasets.

Details

A location is a local folder or a Google Cloud Storage address of the form gs://bucket/prefix. When primary is NULL, the addresses come from the environment variables <env>_PRIMARY and <env>_SECONDARY; the second may hold several addresses separated by ;. <env>_SECONDARY is read only when both primary and secondary are NULL, so that a primary given in the call is never mixed with secondaries of another store.

  • A primary that cannot be reached aborts, with the credentials each client of its backend needs.

  • A secondary that cannot be reached gives a warning and is marked unavailable: reads and writes skip it until store_refresh() finds it again.

  • A location without catalogs aborts, unless create = TRUE, which initialises it with empty catalogs (as store_create() does, with the store's history default off).

The object has reference semantics: functions that change a location update it in place, so the same object serves several writes in a row. Read functions use the catalogs held by the object; call store_refresh() to see what other sessions wrote since.

See also

store_create(), store_refresh(), store_datasets(), store_status(), rcs_auth_gcs().

Examples

primary <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-connect")
st <- store_connect(primary, create = TRUE)
store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(100, seed = 1), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales", description = "Simulated daily sales.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 100 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-connect  2/2
#>   files sent  23.8 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
st
#> ── rcs store ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Locations:
#>   primary  local  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-connect
#> History: off (store default)
#> Datasets: 1
#>   name     kind   rows     size  files  updated
#>   sales/
#>     daily  table   100  23.8 kB      2  2026-11-27 13:56

# The same, with the address in the environment
withr::with_envvar(c(STORE_PRIMARY = primary), store_connect())
#> ── rcs store ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Locations:
#>   primary  local  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-connect
#> History: off (store default)
#> Datasets: 1
#>   name     kind   rows     size  files  updated
#>   sales/
#>     daily  table   100  23.8 kB      2  2026-11-27 13:56
unlink(primary, recursive = TRUE)
